text: The dispute intake of rwb-comms is the operation POST /cases/{caseId}/disputes and the read GET /disputes/{disputeId} under /api/recovery/comms/v1, with the DisputeRequest and DisputeAnswer shapes and the dispute_intake table of section 11 of RWB-P6-E4038-APP.
why: No source names a dispute operation, a request, an answer or a table for rwb-comms, and FEAT-COM-04 asks for the outcome only, so the elements that carry it are fixed by the contract baseline and their field types are left to its review.
read: FSD P6 A2.17; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 and T3.1; legacy RWB-E4-038
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-comms at the contract baseline review
impact: The paths, the shapes and the table are fixed for the app story to build against on Day 1; a change after sign-off needs a new major version.

text: The principal of a self-service dispute is the authenticated customer of LINE OA or HOME.SCB, passed by gateway-bff with the case scope and a short-lived token; a customer row of TSD P6 T6.1 is not needed, and the capability area and the coarse permission stay gateway-bff's.
why: FEAT-COM-04 is a customer action on the bank's digital channels, and TSD P6 T6.1 lists staff and partner roles only, so the action has no Workbench role to hold its right.
read: FSD P6 A2.17.3.3 and A2.17.2 (Integration points LINE OA, HOME.SCB); TSD P6 v2 T6.1; Architecture v5 slide 8
confirm: Platform route owner and the security architect
impact: The story declares no P4 dependency and no role table; object-level authorisation is the case scope passed by gateway-bff.

text: X1 is opened in rwb-deviation through its contract with code X1, the case, the dispute reference, the channel principal and the owner and same-day service level of R-DEV-01 and R-DEV-02; the open and the state read are consumed on a fake and add no dependency row.
why: The deviation record, its owner, its clock and its outcome are rwb-deviation's under R-UNI-04, R-DEV-01 and R-DEV-02, and no source publishes an operation that opens X1 for a customer dispute.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-04, R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02, R-DEV-09, R-DEV-18; FSD P6 A2.17
confirm: rwb-deviation owner at the contract baseline review
impact: The intake fails safe: a failed deviation call keeps the contact stop applied and leaves the intake in RECEIVED with a retry and an alert.

text: The dispute reason codes, the decision code and the rule id of a dispute are reference data or parameters read with the version in force, not constants of the code or of the contract.
why: BR-P6-017 forbids writing in code any value a business person may change, and no source gives the code list or the decision code of FEAT-COM-04.
read: FSD P6 A2.17.3.1 (BR-P6-017, VR-P6-017-1, VR-P6-017-2); Template and Rules §R7.2 s17
confirm: Business lead and the configuration owner at the wave 3 readiness review
impact: A new reason code or a new decision code is a data row, not a release.

text: The legacy rows of RWB-E4-038 that name SCR-33 Template approval, Litigation C and Litigation R, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} belong to the notice and template features of this service; the dispute screen is the customer's channel behind gateway-bff.
why: The legacy story body describes a customer self-service dispute while its own screen, permission and endpoint tables describe the notice and template administration, and the higher sources place those rows in the notice feature.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-038 Screen and states, Permission checks, Endpoints; FSD P6 A2.17 and A1.2; TSD P6 v2 T6.1
confirm: Business analyst, P6, at the story review
impact: No notice or template row is copied into the dispute story, and the Litigation rights are not claimed for a customer action.

text: The contract baseline fixes the two dispute operations, the DisputeRequest and DisputeAnswer shapes, the three dispute states and the dispute_intake table, and leaves the field types, the request body detail and the decision code to the baseline review.
why: No source names a dispute operation, a shape, a state vocabulary or a table, so the baseline is the only place they can be fixed before the app story starts.
read: FSD P6 A2.17; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1, T3.1 and T6.1; legacy RWB-E4-038
confirm: Consumer sign-off at the contract baseline review
impact: The app story and the fakes are bound to these paths and states; a breaking change needs a new major version.

text: The deviation open and the deviation read of rwb-deviation are declared as consumed rows with the placeholder path, request and answer, and their fake is derived from R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02 and R-UNI-04.
why: X1 and its outcome are rwb-deviation's, and no source publishes an operation that opens or reads a deviation for a customer dispute.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-04, R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02; Ownership Map
confirm: rwb-deviation owner at the contract baseline review
impact: The consumed rows are built against a fake and carry the placeholder until the rwb-deviation owner publishes the operation.

text: The legacy rows of RWB-E4-038 that belong to the notice and template features are named as that feature's in the baseline and are copied into no criterion; the contract declares no Litigation right and no SCR-33 screen.
why: The higher sources place the notice operations, the template screen and the Litigation rights in the notice and template features, so a dispute contract that claimed them would duplicate another owner's element.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-038 Screen and states, Permission checks, Endpoints; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1
confirm: Business analyst, P6, and the solution architect
impact: The baseline holds no role table and no screen, and the notice contract keeps its own rows unchanged.

text: The session, the scope and the coarse permission of both dispute operations are declared as gateway-bff's, asked of rwb-access, and the baseline declares no P4 dependency and no role or scope table of its own.
why: The principal of the action is a customer of the bank's digital channels and no Workbench role describes it, so the authorise decision belongs to the route and to the access contract.
read: Architecture v5 slide 8 and slide 10 notes; TSD P6 v2 T6.2; RWB-PLT-N001-CON
confirm: Platform route owner and the security architect
impact: A refusal is declared as 401 or 404 with the platform envelope, and the contract holds no role list to keep in step.
